observations: Official jsDelivr documentation states that GitHub files can be loaded by exact commit SHA with /gh/user/repo@version/file and gives a full commit-hash example.
The same documentation states that GitHub files are kept in permanent S3 storage, but are fetched directly from GitHub on the first request (or when S3 is unavailable).

That lazy origin-fetch property means a successful jsDelivr GET does not by itself prove that an independent third party possessed the target object before the probe; the retrieval may populate jsDelivr from GitHub at request time.

The current scheduled-Chat web surface could not directly open the exact target jsDelivr URL because arbitrary unindexed target URLs are blocked by the web safety/navigation layer, so the target SHA was not independently observed from jsDelivr in this bounded slice.

The documented CDN path is anonymous static HTTP and requires no user account or paid query execution; no finite monthly/trial/paid quota or incremental monetary cost was identified or consumed in this slice.
